stem: The table shows the 100 players registered at a cricket academy in Karachi, by age group and main playing role. If a player who is not a batter is selected at random, what is the probability that the player is in the 16 and over age group?

figure.title: Players by age group and role

solution: Players who are not batters are the bowlers and all-rounders: \(40 + 20 = 60\) players.
Of these, the 16 and over players number \(26 + 12 = 38\).

explanation.A: Correct. Of the 60 players who are not batters, \(26 + 12 = 38\) are 16 and over.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This divides by all 100 players instead of only the 60 players who are not batters.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This counts only the bowlers who are 16 and over and leaves out the 12 all-rounders.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the probability that a batter is 16 and over: the wrong group of players.

verify:
r = {row[0]: [int(v) for v in row[1:]] for row in figure['rows']}
not_bat = r['Total'][1] + r['Total'][2]
old = r['16 and over'][1] + r['16 and over'][2]
p = Rational(old, not_bat)
assert p == Rational(19, 30)
assert value(choices[answer]) == p
assert all(value(choices[k]) != p for k in choices if k != answer)
